title: ⚔️ Boss: tenses and degrees in one story

questions.prompt:
In the school magazine, a pupil interviews Mr Hamadi, the baker. Complete the pupil's question.

"What time (you / open) ___ your bakery every morning?"
questions.explanation: "Every morning" shows a habit, so the question is in the present simple. A question in the present simple needs the auxiliary before the subject: "do" with you, "does" only with he, she or it, and the verb then stays in its base form. The continuous is for an action happening now, not for a habit.

questions.prompt:
A school magazine describes Mr Hamadi's bakery. Complete the sentence.

"The crust of the new loaf is (soft) ___ the crust of the old one."
questions.explanation: Soft is a short adjective, so the comparison takes -er: "softer", not "more soft". Two crusts are compared, so "than" must come before the second one; without it, nothing links the new crust to the old one.

questions.prompt:
A school magazine describes Mr Hamadi's bakery. Complete the sentence.

"His grandfather (build) ___ the first oven of the bakery in 1962."
questions.explanation: "In 1962" is a finished time, so the verb is in the simple past. Build is irregular: its past form is not made with -ed.

questions.prompt:
A school magazine describes Mr Hamadi's bakery. Complete the sentence.

"The local newspaper (take) ___ many photos of the bakery lately."
questions.explanation: "Lately" links the action to today and gives no finished time, so the verb is in the present perfect: have or has, then the past participle. The newspaper is one thing (it), so the auxiliary is "has". Take is irregular: its past participle is "taken", while "took" is its simple past.

questions.prompt:
A school magazine describes Mr Hamadi's bakery. Complete the sentence.

"Mr Hamadi usually (bake) ___ (small) ___ loaves for the school canteen than for his shop." Choose the correct pair.
questions.explanation: "Usually" shows a habit, so the verb is in the present simple, and Mr Hamadi is one person (he): "bakes", with its -s. Small is a short adjective: its comparative is "smaller", and "than" introduces the second thing compared. "More" goes only before a long adjective.

questions.prompt:
A school magazine describes Mr Hamadi's bakery. Complete the sentence.

"Before 2015, the street (have) ___ five bakeries. Today, Mr Hamadi's is (traditional) ___ of them all." Choose the correct pair.
questions.explanation: "Before 2015" is a finished time, so the first verb is in the simple past. "Of them all" puts one bakery at the top of a group, so the superlative is needed, with "the" in front of it. Traditional is a long adjective: it takes "the most", not -est.

questions.prompt: A school magazine describes Mr Hamadi's bakery. Which sentences are correct?

options.text: Mr Hamadi's niece helps in the bakery every Saturday.
The bakery has won a prize in 2019.
His loaves are more expensive than the loaves at the supermarket.
Of all our bakers, Mr Hamadi is more patient.
Yesterday, a journalist has visited the shop.
The bakery has just opened a second shop.

questions.explanation: The habit with "every Saturday" takes the present simple with its -s; two kinds of loaf compared take "more ... than"; "just" goes with the present perfect. The others break a rule: a present perfect cannot take a finished time such as 2019 or yesterday, and a comparison with a whole group ("Of all our bakers") needs the superlative, not "more" alone.
